Note on comparability: Alaska Air Group's FY2024 results are not fully comparable to prior years or to the other four carriers because they include only a partial-year (post-September 18, 2024) consolidation of Hawaiian Holdings following that acquisition, which contributed $869M revenue and a $113M net loss to Alaska's consolidated results [DOC] "On September 18, 2024, Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings... For the period from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024, revenue and net loss from Hawaiian recognized... was $869 million and $113 million, respectively." This does not change the ranking outcome, but it means Alaska's net income figure reflects a different consolidated entity structure than in prior periods.

All five figures are otherwise reported on the same FY2024 (calendar year) GAAP basis from each company's 10-K, so Delta's and United's results are directly comparable to each other and to American, Southwest, and Alaska (with the caveat above for Alaska).

Delta Air Lines had the highest net income among the five carriers in FY2024.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines (net income of $3,457 million in FY2024, the highest among Delta, United, Southwest, American, and Alaska)
